comparisons.peer_topic: Competitive landscape and determinants of product competitiveness
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD operates in a highly competitive market where timely delivery of latest products is critical for revenue growth. Key factors determining product competitiveness include total cost of ownership, performance, features (including AI accelerations), energy efficiency, and software compatibility.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD define product competitiveness through similar technical metrics: performance, power, and total cost of ownership. Intel explicitly states its objective is to improve user experiences through advances in 'performance, power, cost, connectivity, security, form factor,' while AMD lists 'total cost of ownership,' 'performance,' 'energy efficiency,' and 'form factor' as main determinants. However, AMD emphasizes 'timely product introductions' and 'software compatibility' as critical competitive factors, whereas Intel focuses more on internal operational efficiency goals like 'reducing design complexity' and 're-using IP.'

sentences.text: Our objective with each new generation of products is to improve user experiences and value through advances in performance, power, cost, connectivity, security, form factor, and other features.
We also focus on reducing our design complexity, re-using IP, and increasing ecosystem collaboration to improve our efficiency.
The markets in which our products are sold are highly competitive and delivering the latest and best products to market on a timely basis is critical to achieving revenue growth.

We believe that the main factors that determine our product competitiveness are total cost of ownership, timely product introductions, product quality, product features and capabilities (including accelerations for key workloads such as AI), energy efficiency (including power consumption and battery life, given their impact on total cost of ownership), reliability, performance, size (or form factor), selling price, cost, adherence to industry standards (and the creation of open industry standards), level of integration, software and hardware compatibility, ease of use and functionality of software design tools, completeness of applicable software solutions, security and stability, brand recognition and availability.

peer_results.rationale: The provided candidates for AVGO (Tanzu Software Portfolio and VeloRAIN AI) focus on application development platforms, software governance, and specific workload security rather than the hardware product competitiveness, architectural strategy, or device-level user experience improvements that characterize Intel's Item 1 disclosure. AVGO's software-centric focus does not match the hardware/platform-centric 'product competitiveness' strategy described by Intel.

comparisons.peer_summary: Micron makes significant investments in proprietary product and process technology to increase bit density and reduce costs, introducing new generations with improved performance characteristics such as higher data transfer rates, advanced packaging, lower power consumption, and increased memory density.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron frame their competitive strategy around significant investment in proprietary technology to drive generational improvements in performance, power efficiency, and cost. Intel states it has 'intensified our focus and investment on areas key to product competitiveness' to improve user experience via 'performance, power, cost.' Similarly, Micron states it 'makes significant investments to develop proprietary product and process technology' to 'reduce per-bit manufacturing costs' and introduce products with 'improved performance characteristics' including 'lower power consumption.' Both companies view technological advancement and cost reduction as the primary drivers of competitiveness.

sentences.text: We have intensified our focus and investment on areas key to product competitiveness.
Our objective with each new generation of products is to improve user experiences and value through advances in performance, power, cost, connectivity, security, form factor, and other features.

We make significant investments to develop proprietary product and process technology, which generally increases bit density per wafer and reduces per-bit manufacturing costs of each generation of product.

We continue to introduce new generations of products that offer improved performance characteristics, including higher data transfer rates, advanced packaging solutions, lower power consumption, improved read/write reliability, and increased memory density.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA's key strategy involves advancing its accelerated computing platform to solve complex problems with higher performance and lower power consumption than alternatives. This full-stack innovation approach leverages GPUs, CUDA, and networking technologies to serve diverse end markets including Data Center, Gaming, Professional Visualization, and Automotive.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and NVIDIA both articulate a strategy focused on delivering superior performance and efficiency through deep architectural and software integration. Intel highlights 'xPU across a diverse mix of... architectures... enabled by a scalable software stack and integrated into systems by advanced packaging technology' to improve user experiences. NVIDIA describes its 'accelerated computing platform' strategy to solve complex problems with 'higher performance and lower power consumption' using a 'full-stack innovation approach' across 'architecture, chip design, system, interconnect, and software layers.' Both firms emphasize a holistic, multi-layered approach to computing rather than single-component improvements.

sentences.text: We believe the future is with xPU across a diverse mix of scalar, vector, matrix, and spatial architectures deployed in CPU, GPU, NPU, IPU, accelerators, and FPGA sockets, enabled by a scalable software stack and integrated into systems by advanced packaging technology.
Our objective with each new generation of products is to improve user experiences and value through advances in performance, power, cost, connectivity, security, form factor, and other features.
Our accelerated computing platform can solve complex problems in significantly less time and with lower power consumption than alternative computational approaches.
We work to deliver continued performance leaps that outpace Moore's Law by leveraging innovation across the architecture, chip design, system, interconnect, and software layers.

The programmable nature of our architecture allows us to make leveraged investments in research and development: we can support several multi-billion-dollar end markets with shared underlying technology by using a variety of software stacks developed either internally or by third-party developers and partners.

comparisons.peer_topic: Strategic focus on intelligent computing and AI innovation
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm states that worldwide demand for intelligent computing requires continuous innovation to improve user experiences and expand on-device AI capabilities at low power, supported by significant history of R&D investment and intellectual property development.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm link product competitiveness to continuous innovation in intelligent computing and on-device AI capabilities to enhance user experience. Intel aims to improve user experiences through advances in 'performance, power, cost... and security' within its xPU vision. Qualcomm states that demand for 'intelligent computing everywhere requires continuous innovation to improve user experiences... expand on-device processing and AI capabilities at low power.' Both companies explicitly tie their competitive positioning to the evolution of on-device AI and intelligent computing architectures.

sentences.text: Our objective with each new generation of products is to improve user experiences and value through advances in performance, power, cost, connectivity, security, form factor, and other features.

We believe the future is with xPU across a diverse mix of scalar, vector, matrix, and spatial architectures deployed in CPU, GPU, NPU, IPU, accelerators, and FPGA sockets, enabled by a scalable software stack and integrated into systems by advanced packaging technology.

The worldwide demand for intelligent computing everywhere requires continuous innovation to improve user experiences, support new services, expand on-device processing and AI capabilities at low power, and increase wireless connectivity capacity and performance.
To meet these requirements, different foundational technologies, including wireless communications, computing (including on-device AI), multimedia and location, continue to evolve.
